title: Unknown-check closures are matched by runtime key only: a reused key can turn an unrelated end into a misleading late-end notice
outcome: A check closed with outcome Unknown at a turn boundary is told a late end only for its own command invocation. An end from a later command that reuses the runtime key (Codex's command-text fallback, or another command) never consumes the closure or publishes a late-end line naming the old check. Both closing boundaries close consistently, and both have tests.
acceptance: A command start that reuses the key of a retained unended-check closure retires that closure (or the closure carries a start identity that the end must match), so the reused command's completion publishes no late-end line. The real late end of the closed check is still told once when it arrives before any reuse.

The turn's Fresh close and its clear of the live checks agree. Either the close also closes unended checks of other grants before clearing all checks, or a comment with file:line records why no other grant's check can be present.

Tests cover: close A with no end, then a later command B reusing A's key (a non-check command, and a check that ends, including a duplicate completion), with no late-end line naming A; and the next-turn-start boundary closing an unended check that a Cached or Skipped close left, once.
disposal_reason: Superseded by the landed triple commit 23e77889, which delivers the unended-check closure and late-end behavior in w-aec234; the replacement item completed with its passing evaluation on that same commit.
